successCriteria.description: ILeaveService exposes create(input), submit(id), approve(id), reject(id), cancel(id), each returning Promise<LeaveRequestView>, and LeaveService implements each by delegating verbatim to the matching IApiClient method (createLeave/submitLeave/approveLeave/rejectLeave/cancelLeave) with the exact argument and returning the API client's value unchanged.
Each write method propagates an ApiError thrown by the API client unchanged (same instance, no wrapping/transformation), with no lifecycle or extra logic in the service.

getAvailableLeaveActions(status, role, isOwner) returns string[] per the matrix: owner → ['submit'] when DRAFT, ['cancel'] when DRAFT or SUBMITTED; MANAGER/ADMIN → ['approve','reject'] when SUBMITTED; empty array for every other combination. It is pure (no I/O, no imports beyond the enums).

validateLeaveRequestInput(input) enforces exactly three rules and returns an array of human-readable error strings (empty when valid): both startDate and endDate non-empty; endDate not before startDate compared as calendar-date strings; leaveTypeCode chosen. It must not mirror min-notice/max-duration policy and must fetch nothing.
web/src/modules/leave/index.ts re-exports getAvailableLeaveActions and validateLeaveRequestInput alongside the existing service exports, so pages can import them from the module entry point.

The extended vitest suite covers: each write method delegates to the matching apiClient method with the right argument and returns the value unchanged; each propagates an ApiError unchanged (including a rejected create); getAvailableLeaveActions owner submit/cancel, manager approve/reject, and forbidden combinations returning empty; validateLeaveRequestInput missing dates, end-before-start, missing type, and the valid case returning empty.

constraints: The service write methods must contain no lifecycle/state-transition logic — they delegate verbatim to the IApiClient and return its value unchanged; ApiError propagates unchanged (no catch/wrap/transform).

getAvailableLeaveActions and validateLeaveRequestInput must be pure functions: no I/O, no network, no Date-object construction for comparison (calendar-date string comparison), and no imports beyond the shared enums/types.

validateLeaveRequestInput must enforce ONLY the three spec rules (both dates non-empty, endDate not before startDate as calendar dates, leaveTypeCode chosen) and must NOT mirror backend min-notice or max-duration policy.
No changes to IApiClient/ApiClient or shared types are permitted this phase — the five write methods and CreateLeaveRequestInput DTO already exist from Phase 1 and are consumed as-is.
outOfScope: Backend policy enforcement (min-notice, max-duration, sufficiency/balance checks) — validation is client-side shape/date/type only.
Page/UI work (RequestLeavePage, LeaveDetailPage, LeaveListPage, App.tsx routing) — deferred to Phases 3–5.
Any changes to the API client transport layer or shared types (already delivered in Phase 1).

entityInvariants.invariant: The service is a thin delegation boundary over IApiClient: every method (read and write) returns the API client's value unchanged and propagates ApiError unchanged; it owns no lifecycle/state-transition logic.

Pure status+role action matrix: owner may submit (DRAFT) and cancel (DRAFT or SUBMITTED); MANAGER/ADMIN may approve/reject (SUBMITTED); any other combination yields an empty array. Deterministic and side-effect free.

Pure validator returning string[] of human-readable errors (empty when valid); enforces exactly three rules (both dates non-empty, endDate >= startDate as calendar-date strings, leaveTypeCode chosen) and never fetches or applies backend policy.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Delegates verbatim to apiClient.createLeave(input); propagates ApiError unchanged.
Delegates verbatim to apiClient.submitLeave(id); propagates ApiError unchanged.
Delegates verbatim to apiClient.approveLeave(id); propagates ApiError unchanged.
Delegates verbatim to apiClient.rejectLeave(id); propagates ApiError unchanged.
Delegates verbatim to apiClient.cancelLeave(id); propagates ApiError unchanged.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The five write methods must match the exact signatures already declared on IApiClient (createLeave(input), submitLeave(id), approveLeave(id), rejectLeave(id), cancelLeave(id)) and delegate to them verbatim.

CreateLeaveRequestInput (leaveTypeCode: LeaveTypeCode; startDate: string; endDate: string) and the LeaveStatus/EmployeeRole/LeaveTypeCode enums must be imported from shared types, not re-declared locally.
The existing read methods (list/getById) and their verbatim-delegation + ApiError-propagation pattern must be preserved; new write methods follow the same delegation style.
The existing makeApiClient test helper already stubs all five write methods; the extended suite must reuse it and follow the established vitest style (vi.fn, rejects.toBe for ApiError identity).

integrationPoints.why: The service write methods delegate to the five IApiClient write methods delivered in Phase 1.
CreateLeaveRequestInput, LeaveStatus, EmployeeRole, LeaveTypeCode, and LeaveRequestView are the types consumed by the service and helpers.
The module entry point must re-export the new helpers so Phases 3–4 pages can import them.
